agree.reason: The calm tone, the 74-household figure and four concrete, cheap-to-grant requests give a skeptical manager an easy way to act, although announcing the TV station may make her defensive.

honest.reason: Nearly every claim tracks the brief, and the derived ratios hold up, though 'one day in every eight' depends on how much of the year has passed and the walker scenario is an inference rather than a reported fact.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the raw numbers into telling forms ('one day in every eight', 'two in every three apartments', the June estimate implying an August arrival) but does not combine the 23 elderly and 6 mobility-limited residents into a share of the building.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is shown accurately as a repeating six-to-eight-week promise that has already slipped once, but the letter does not spell out what another missed estimate would add to the outage count.

qualification.reason: The requests are checkable (named supplier, confirmed date, updates every two weeks), but the reply deadline and notice window are left as placeholders and nothing is said about what happens if they are missed.

objections.reason: It anticipates the passing certificate, the $400,000 infeasibility claim and the 'few loud people' view (74 of 112 households) without raising any objection that the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted open letter of about 420 words that works both in a lobby and for the media.
